The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10045 at 14 FR 1227 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed March 15, 1949; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the March 18, 1949 issue. Inventory corrected: one clause, offsets 2034 to 2876 of the held text, from the enacting words to the last operative sentence; the dossier's two spans begin at the heading and then run on into unrelated page text after the order ends. The order's heading and recitals precede it in the held text and contain no command. Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the Wabash Railroad Company and the Ann Arbor Railroad Company, carriers, and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers, the Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen and Enginemen, the Order of Railway Conductors and the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, labor organizations. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the Wabash Railroad Company and the Ann Arbor Railroad Company or their employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 10045 describes creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy for Emergency Board No. 71 (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10045_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10045_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_40f7c1ee3a.txt, a held text lead taken from a scan's text layer and not an authenticated original) is the board's report to the President. Its cover is dated April 6 (the text layer garbles the year digits; the board was appointed March 15, 1949 by this order), and its transmittal letter to the President, dated at St. Louis on April 6 and signed by the board's chairman and two members, submits the board's report as an emergency board designated under Executive Order 10045. The report recites that the board, at the parties' request, stood by until April 4, 1949, when the parties appeared in open session and reported full, complete and final disposition and settlement of all matters in dispute, evidenced by a written agreement signed on April 4, 1949; it therefore reports a settlement and makes no recommendations on the merits. The board's report to the President is accordingly dated April 6, 1949 (the date the parties reported settlement was April 4, 1949), and the standstill, which ran until thirty days after that report, ran to about May 6, 1949. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C) the report deadline and the standstill are not ends: the order was functionally spent on April 6, 1949, when the board made its report, and its standstill period lapsed about thirty days later. It stayed on the books until the express revocation. The dossier has no citable record covering this passage, so it is stated here and not entered as a later event. Prior research: the packet locates earlier unfiled versions of this claim in another batch folder; independent review rejected them before filing (a defect in the description of the board's report, now corrected). They were read as drafts and not as evidence; no canonical claim, status hold or conflicting version exists for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning; they are the packet's machine searches.
